title: Add source-backed editing and server sync
description:
Note: Editing and work for this PR was done with AI. You are welcome to review and/or merge (would recommend using AI) or not! These are changes I made which greatly streamlined my own editing experience for presentations. A remaining/future challenge is how to better enable parallel editing (LLM developing slides on the backend as user tweaks UX in foreground). Right now, the user gets an error if they try to save changes back to server from an outdated version.

### Summary
This PR adds richer editing capabilities to the Quarto Revealjs editable extension, including source-backed text and SVG editing, undo/redo improvements, and saving changes back to the owning QMD file.

### Changes

- Add source-backed editing for text, positioned media, and SVG elements.
- Improve slide-to-source mapping, including support for vertical and cloned slides.
- Add a presentation edit server that applies revision-checked changes, preserves includes, creates backups, and re-renders the presentation.
- Improve undo/redo and element reactivation.
- Add installation tooling and JavaScript and Python tests.

### Testing
JavaScript and Python tests were added or updated; they have not been run as part of this change.

title: modify-mode: Escape to exit, aria-labels on rings, focus restore
description:
## Summary
- Pressing `Escape` while modify mode is active exits modify mode and returns focus to the Modify toolbar button. Escape is ignored while a heading is being edited inline so the existing revert-on-Escape behavior is preserved.
- Valid elements get `aria-label="Click to modify (<type>)"`; warn elements get `aria-label="Cannot modify: <reason>"`. The element's original `aria-label`/`alt` is saved and restored when modify mode exits or re-classifies (e.g. slide change).
- After finishing an inline title edit (blur), focus returns to the Modify toolbar button instead of being left on the (now non-editable) heading.

Closes part of the modify-mode accessibility audit — keyboard exit + ARIA labeling + focus restoration.

## Test plan
- [x] `npm run test:run` — 207 unit tests pass
- [x] `npx playwright test e2e/modify-mode.spec.js` — 22/22 pass on Chromium and Firefox, including two new cases:
  - Escape exits modify mode and focuses `.toolbar-modify`
  - Valid elements expose `aria-label` matching `Click to modify`, removed on exit
- [ ] Manual screen-reader smoke test (VoiceOver) to confirm announcements read naturally

title: Extract anchor-resolution and wrapper helpers (PR 3)
description:
## Summary

Third step of the modify-mode dedup plan. Stacks on top of #149.

Three new helpers replace duplicated logic in the Code blocks, Tables, Equations, Code chunk outputs, and Code chunk figures classifiers:

- **\`findTopLevelWrappers(slideEl, innerSelector, { preFilter, postFilter })\`** — replaces the \`topLevelAncestorIn\` + seen-set + filter-chain pattern. preFilter handles tables-inside-\`div.cell\` skip; postFilter handles code blocks rejecting \`div.cell\` and equations requiring \`isDisplayEquationContainer\`.
- **\`resolveByHeader({ chunkEls, sources, getHeader, headerAttr, idxAttr })\`** — header-line anchor with positional fallback. Used by Tables + Equations.
- **\`resolveByLabel(el, sources, { getLabel, getFirstLine, … })\`** — label match with positional fallback guarded by a first-line sanity check. Used by Code chunk outputs + Code chunk figures.

\`topLevelAncestorIn\` is now exported.

\`modify-mode.js\`: 3149 → 3169 lines. The classifier bodies shrink but helper definitions + JSDoc grow more; the win here is centralising four duplicated anchor-resolution policies into one place, not raw line count.

## Test plan

- [x] \`npm run test:run\` — 207 unit tests pass (14 new helper tests for resolveByHeader, resolveByLabel, findTopLevelWrappers, topLevelAncestorIn)
- [x] \`testing/run-tests.sh\` — all 37 shell tests pass
- [x] \`npm run test:e2e\` — 851 E2E pass on Chromium + Firefox (7 skipped)
- [ ] Manual smoke (focus on the affected classifiers): activate one each of Tables, Equations, Code blocks, Code chunk outputs, Code chunk figures; save; diff QMD against \`main\`.

Refs PR 3 step of \`~/Desktop/plans/2026-05-12-modify-mode-dedup.md\`.

title: Merge Images/Videos into makeMediaClassifier factory (PR 2)
description: ## Summary Second step of the modify-mode dedup plan. Stacks on top of #148. The Images and Videos classifiers shared their entire activate + serialize pipeline. Extract a `makeMediaClassifier({ tagName, label, getSrc, setupFn, classify, beforeSetup, cleanup })` factory and register both through it. Videos-specific bookkeeping moves into hooks: - `classify` — owns the per-element decision (Images: multi-figure chunk warn; Videos: `controls` removal for Firefox's click-intercept issue). - `beforeSetup(el)` — runs after dataset stamping, before `setupFn`. Videos clears Reveal's `max-width: 95%` and opts the activated video out of the pending controls-restore set. - `cleanup()` — restores `controls` on previously-stripped videos when modify mode exits without activation. `src/modify-mode.js`: 3175 → 3149 lines. Cross-shape byte-equality assertion added in new `src/__tests__/modify-mode-media.test.js`. ## Test plan - [x] `npm run test:run` — 193 unit tests pass (4 new media-factory tests including the cross-shape equality assertion) - [x] `testing/run-tests.sh` — all 37 shell tests pass - [x] `npm run test:e2e` — 851 E2E pass on Chromium + Firefox (7 skipped) - [ ] **Manual smoke (Firefox required)**: render `basic.qmd`, in modify mode: - [ ] Activate an `` — drag/resize/save, diff QMD against `main` - [ ] Activate a `

title: Dedup modify-mode classifier boilerplate (PR 1 / mechanical)
description:
## Summary

First mechanical step of the modify-mode dedup plan. Extracts six shared helpers used across the 12 classifiers in `src/modify-mode.js`. Behavior-preserving.

- `escapeRegex` → `src/utils.js` (was duplicated in `modify-mode.js` and `modify-mode-positioned.js`).
- `captureSlideRelativePosition(el, { rectSource })` — replaces ~7 inline copies of the `slideEl` / `getSlideScale` / `getBoundingClientRect` dance. `rectSource` lets the equation classifier anchor on the inner math node.
- `lockNaturalDimensions(el, displayOverride)` — now used by lists/blockquotes, code blocks, code-chunk outputs, and tables (previously inline).
- `sortByIndexAttr(els, attrName)` — replaces 8 per-classifier sort-by-dataset-index blocks.
- `forEachInReverse(items, fn)` — names the bottom-to-top splice idiom used by 5 serialize() paths.
- `groupModifiedElementsByChunk(els, text)` — replaces the byChunk Map construction at the top of 8 serialize() methods.

`modify-mode.js`: 3294 → 3175 lines (-119 net; classifier bodies shrink more, helpers add ~120 lines of definitions+JSDoc).

## Test plan

- [x] `npm run test:run` — 189 unit tests pass, including 24 new helper tests
- [x] `testing/run-tests.sh` — all 37 shell tests pass
- [x] `npm run test:e2e` — 851 E2E tests pass on Chromium + Firefox (7 skipped)
- [ ] Manual smoke: render `basic.qmd`, click one element of each classifier type in modify mode, save, diff QMD against `main` (see plan §Manual smoke)

Refs the PR 1 step of `~/Desktop/plans/2026-05-12-modify-mode-dedup.md`.

- https://github.com/mcanouil/quarto-extensions/tree/quarto-tests/logs/emilhvitfeldt/quarto-revealjs-editable

title: Feat/unsaved changes toolbar
description: This Pull Request follows PR #22, which was a bugfix pull request. It therefore includes all the commits proposed in that PR. The present PR is a feature / UI improvement that makes the save and copy actions discoverable: a floating toolbar slides in from the bottom of the presentation whenever an editable element is modified, so users no longer need to know about the hidden buttons in the Tools menu. ## Problem The "Save Edits" and "Copy to clipboard" actions are hidden inside the Tools menu — the user has to know they exist. There is no visual feedback indicating that unsaved modifications are pending. ## Solution Adds a non-intrusive floating toolbar that slides in from the bottom of the presentation whenever an editable element is modified (drag, resize, or text size / layout edit). The toolbar is only shown when modifications are actually made — it never appears if no `{.editable}` elements are present in the document (this is guaranteed by the conditional injection introduced in PR #22: the JS is not even loaded when there are no editable elements). The toolbar shows: - An animated yellow dot and "unsaved changes" label while modifications are pending - A "📋 Copy to clipboard" button - A "💾 Save edits" button - A × button for manual dismissal After a successful action: - **Save**: dot turns green, label becomes "downloaded! → replace your original .qmd if satisfied", toolbar slides out after 3.5s - **Copy**: dot turns green, label becomes "copied! → paste into your .qmd to apply changes", toolbar slides out after 3.5s ## Changes - `_extensions/editable/editable.js` — floating toolbar IIFE + hooks into drag, resize, text edit, save and copy actions ## Related Complements #8 (clipboard support added in PR #22). See annotated screenshot taken during testing / development :

title: fix: add defensive null checks for global variables
description:
## Bug
https://github.com/EmilHvitfeldt/quarto-revealjs-editable/issues/83 — Several places in the source assume global variables exist without null checks, causing uncaught runtime errors that break the editor.

## Fix
Three guards, matching the locations described in the issue:

1. **`main.js` — `getEditableFilename()`**: Return `'untitled.qmd'` when `window._input_filename` is undefined instead of throwing on `.split()`
2. **`utils.js` — `getCurrentSlideIndex()` and `hasTitleSlide()`**: Check `typeof Reveal === 'undefined'` before accessing `Reveal.getIndices()` / `Reveal.getSlide()`, returning safe defaults (`0` / `false`)
3. **`arrows.js` — `onDrag()`**: Guard against null `arrowData.element` before calling `getBoundingClientRect()` (element may have been removed)

## Testing
Verified each guard handles the undefined case gracefully without breaking the normal flow when globals are present.

Happy to address any feedback.

Greetings, saschabuehrle

description:
Adds Quarto Wizard support files for `editable` to improve authoring and make usage less error-prone in VSCode/Positron when using Quarto Wizard.

### What this adds
- `_extensions/editable/_schema.yml` with class and attribute schema for editable content and saved absolute positioning (`width`, `height`, `left`, `top`, `style`).
- `_extensions/editable/_snippets.json` with practical snippets for setup metadata, editable image markup, and editable text blocks.

### Why this helps
- Provides clearer completion and hover guidance for extension-specific classes and saved attributes.
- Speeds up onboarding by inserting correct revealjs plugin and filter setup.
- Reduces authoring mistakes for editable block and image syntax.

- Snippet specification: https://m.canouil.dev/quarto-wizard/reference/snippet-specification.html

title: Fix: use base64 encoding in Lua filter to prevent qmd content leaking into slides
description:
Closes #21, and after verification, also closes #15, closes #16, should close #13 and close #14 (not verified, I only use macOS and Linux, but I guess the root cause is exactly the same as the other issues). In the meantime, while testing if everything was OK, I really wished the feature request #8 to be solved, so I handled it also 🤣

This is almost a strike 😂 if we were playing bowling

## What lead me to this PR: #21 Problem

When the document YAML contains `include-in-header` with a `<script>` block, the Lua filter injects `window._input_file` via `doc.blocks:insert(pandoc.RawBlock(...))` at the end of the document. Pandoc places this RawBlock outside any Reveal.js `<section>`, causing the raw qmd source to be rendered as visible text in the slides.

A previous workaround using `quarto.doc.include_text("in-header", ...)` also failed, as Quarto passes the content through the Pandoc parser, which interprets parts of the qmd source as Markdown.

## Fix

**`editable.lua`**: Pandoc AST walkers (`Div`, `Image`) detect elements with class `editable` before doing anything. If none are found, the filter returns immediately — no encoding, no injection. Otherwise, the `.qmd` content is encoded as base64 using a correct RFC 4648 pure Lua implementation, written to a temporary HTML file, and injected into `<head>` via `quarto.doc.include_file("in-header", tmpfile)`, bypassing the Pandoc parser entirely. On the JS side, `atob()` decodes the base64 string at load time.

**`editable.js`**: remove the 4 lines in `saveMovedElts()` that compensated for backslash and trailing-space mangling introduced by the old Lua mechanism. With base64, these compensations are not only unnecessary but harmful. Also adds a "Copy qmd to Clipboard" button (closes #8).

## Changes

- `_extensions/editable/editable.lua` — full rewrite using AST walkers + conditional injection + RFC 4648 base64
- `_extensions/editable/editable.js` — removal of 4 compensation lines + clipboard button
